claims.text: An accelerated two-phase coexistence approach combined with enhanced sampling can predict melting properties of high-melting refractory materials.
The proposed approach can achieve DFT-level accuracy.
The proposed approach can calculate melting temperature, fusion enthalpy, fusion entropy, and volume change at melting.
The proposed approach costs substantially less than full thermodynamic integration.
Full thermodynamic integration via ab initio molecular dynamics can be replaced by accelerated two-phase coexistence simulation with enhanced sampling.
The simulation is conducted near the melting point under conditions where solid and liquid coexist.
The coexistence interface between the solid and melt phases mediates the phase transition through its equilibrium properties.
Direct simulation of coexisting solid and liquid phases bypasses exhaustive thermodynamic integration.
Enhanced sampling explores the relevant phase space more efficiently.
Efficient phase-space exploration reduces computational expense while retaining DFT accuracy.
Predicted melting properties will deviate by no more than approximately 10% from values obtained with traditional full-integration methods.
The proposed method will significantly reduce computational time.
Conventional ab initio free-energy calculations require expensive thermodynamic integration using ab initio molecular dynamics.
Incomplete enhanced sampling may fail to capture subtle anharmonic and interfacial effects under extreme conditions.
The method may have limited accuracy for systems involving complex multiphase interactions beyond simple solid-liquid coexistence.
